newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran to deliver oil under Kazakh swap deal.
newsitem.headline: Iran to deliver oil under Kazakh swap deal.

text.p: Iran will deliver the first cargo of its crude oil to its Kharg Island export terminal in the Gulf next week under a swap deal with Kazakhstan, the Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said on Saturday.
"The first cargo of the Iranian crude is going to be delivered on behalf of Kazakhstan next week," he told reporters on the sidelines of an energy conference in Isfahan.

Under the swap deal agreed last year, Iran would initially refine 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Kazakh crude blended with its own Iran Light crude. After two years, the amount would increase to 120,000 bpd.

In return, landlocked Kazakhstan, which has traditionally relied on neighbouring Russia's pipelines for its exports, would be entitled to the same value of crude at Iranian export terminals in the Gulf or at Iran's storage facilities in Europe.
But the deal has been stalled in a dispute over crude quality to be delivered by tankers to northern Iran across the Caspian Sea, Kazakh officials have said.
The main stumbling bloc was the high concentration of mercaptans in Kazakh oil, they said. Mercaptans are undesirable, foul-smelling sulphur compounds.
Trial shipments of Kazakh oil across the Caspian Sea to an Iranian port -- targeted at two million tonnes a year -- had begun in January.
However, oil shipments to Iran reached only 70,000 tonnes this year and were suspended because of the mercaptans problem.
